candidates.summary: the hot-reload socket now follows the page's host but keeps a hard-coded ws:// scheme, so a gnodev page served over https never hot-reloads
candidates.failure_scenario: gnodev behind a TLS-terminating proxy (staging mode, which keeps the watcher and the injected script on by default per command_staging.go; a Codespaces or ngrok https forward; a local Caddy front): the page at https://<host>/ runs new WebSocket('ws://<host>/_events'), which the browser blocks as mixed content for a non-loopback host, so the developer saves a file and the page never reloads, with only a console error. Deriving the scheme from the page, (location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss://' : 'ws://'), lets the same-origin check the emitter now applies pass through a Host-preserving proxy.
candidates.verify_by: read hotreload.js:8 and command_staging.go defaults (noWatch unset, so middleware injected); headful chromium (xvfb-run) on a page served over https by a local TLS proxy in front of gnodev: console shows a mixed-content block for ws://, no /_events upgrade reaches gnodev
candidates.evidence: hotreload.js:8: const ws = new WebSocket('ws://' + window.location.host + '{{- .Path -}}'); command_staging.go: webListenerAddr 127.0.0.1:8888, staging true, no noWatch override; gnodev serves no TLS itself (grep -i tls/wss in contribs/gnodev/*.go and pkg/emitter: no hit)

candidates.summary: the absent-Origin carve-out assumes non-browser clients send no Origin; Python websocket-client sends its own target as Origin by default and is refused once the list is narrowed, though [] accepts it
candidates.failure_scenario: websocket-client (_handshake.py:98-104) sends 'Origin: http://<host:port>' unless suppress_origin is set. Against a node with cors_allowed_origins = [] that Origin equals Host and gorilla's same-origin check upgrades it; narrow the list to ["https://gno.land"] and the same script gets 403 on /websocket while its HTTP POST still answers. Adding an origin to the list thus revokes a client the empty list served, and the new comment tells the operator such clients send no Origin. Either accept an Origin whose host equals r.Host beside the list (parity with [], giving up the DNS-rebinding refusal only a narrowed list has) or state in the cors_allowed_origins comment that a narrowed list must name what non-browser clients send: a design call for the author.
candidates.verify_by: read site-packages/websocket/_handshake.py:95-104; go test in ./tm2/pkg/bft/rpc/lib/server dialing NewWebsocketManager(funcs, []string{"https://gno.land"}) and NewWebsocketManager(funcs, []string{}) with header Origin: "http://"+listener addr: expect 403 and 101
candidates.evidence: grep -n -i origin websocket/_handshake.py: 98 'if not options.get("suppress_origin"):', 102 'headers.append(f"Origin: https://{hostport}")', 104 'headers.append(f"Origin: http://{hostport}")'; handlers.go:1149 'return r.Header.Get("Origin") == "" || corsValidator.OriginAllowed(r)'
